tooltip.tupenter.tick_scripts_enabled: Master switch. While ON, every script below runs ONCE PER TICK (20x/second) — like being a walking mcfunction file. WARNING: any script that sends a command or chat will absolutely flood the chat on a multiplayer server unless you guard it (#if) or the server has sendCommandFeedback off. Best used with conditional scripts that normally do nothing. /tupenter abort turns this off in an emergency.
tooltip.tupenter.add_script: Adds a new (disabled) script row. WARNING: this reloads the screen — script text edits are kept, but unsaved changes in other tabs are discarded.
tooltip.tupenter.tick_scripts: One script per line — statement forms apply like custom command bodies: /command, #directive, bare text = chat (20x/second — you have been warned). Start a line with // to disable it. Tick scripts never touch your resend history and never print #set notices. A script with an error reports once and is skipped until you edit the list. Examples: #if ($client.nbt.Health$ < 6) (/give @s totem_of_undying) — or — #if ($client.y$ > $maxy$) (/tp @s ~ $maxy$ ~) with $maxy$ set via #set.
option.tupenter.reset_on_new_session: Clear Resend History on New Session
tooltip.tupenter.reset_on_new_session: If enabled, your resend history is automatically cleared when you join a world or server.
tooltip.tupenter.rapid_resend_delay: How many ticks the key must be held before rapid-fire starts. Only applies in Press & Hold mode.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_filter: Controls which types of sent messages are recorded and replayed. Note: Changing this setting will clear your current history.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_mode: Press & Hold: Resend fires while the key is held down. Toggle: Resend fires continuously until the key is pressed again. Off: Disables the resend key.
tooltip.tupenter.message_delay: Ticks to wait between sending each individual message in a batch. Set to 0 for no delay.
tooltip.tupenter.suppress_feedback:
Controls whether command output messages are hidden in your chat while Tupenter is firing.
- Off: Never suppress.
- On: Always suppress while firing.
- Dynamic: Only suppress in Toggle mode, not in Press & Hold. Useful if you want feedback when testing (hold), but silence when running hands-free (toggled on).
Note: suppression is client-side only — the server still processes commands normally.
tooltip.tupenter.pause_tracking: If enabled, newly sent messages will NOT update the resend queue while Tupenter is toggled on. Useful to avoid accidentally changing what is being spammed.
tooltip.tupenter.history_depth: How many of your most recent messages Tupenter tracks as a batch. If above 1, Tupenter will remember the last X messages and resend all of them together each cycle.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_delay: Delay between each full batch of messages.
tooltip.tupenter.batch_mode:
Controls behavior when stopping mid-batch:
- Pause: Resume next time.
- Finish: Complete current batch.
- Interrupt: Stop and reset.
(Batches always complete if Message Delay is 0)
tooltip.tupenter.resend_amount: Tupenter will fire off X times in a single tick. Can cause lag or disconnects with higher values.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_order: Order in which history items in a batch are resent.
tooltip.tupenter.import_history: Copies your current session history into the preset messages list. WARNING: This will reload the screen and discard other unsaved changes!
tooltip.tupenter.permanent_messages: The list of messages or commands Tupenter will send when 'What to Resend' is set to Preset Messages.
tooltip.tupenter.enhanced_command_parsin: Master switch for all Tupenter scripting features (chaining, math, custom commands, /calc). When disabled, Tupenter sends commands exactly as written.
tooltip.tupenter.max_commands_per_tick: How many commands Tupenter may send in a single game tick, across all running scripts. Larger scripts are automatically spread over multiple ticks. Raise this on your own server; lower it if a public server kicks you for spam.
tooltip.tupenter.max_commands_per_script: Upper bound on how many commands one typed line may expand into. A script over the limit is rejected before anything is sent.
tooltip.tupenter.max_concurrent_scripts: How many scripts may be mid-execution at the same time. Mostly relevant when large scripts are spread across ticks. Use /tupenter abort to stop all running scripts.
tooltip.tupenter.command_chaining: Lets Tupenter split lines joined with && and send the pieces in order. Each segment picks its own form: /command, #directive, bare text = chat — so /say ready && weather clear says ready then CHATS the words weather clear. Tupenter still remembers and replays the original combined line as one history entry. Example: /weather clear && /time set day.
tooltip.tupenter.number_math: Evaluates $ ... $ expressions inside commands before sending. Supports math (+, -, *, /, decimals, parentheses, s for stacks x64), text in "quotes", comparisons (==, !=, <, >), conditions like $x > 5 ? "big" : "small"$, and functions: int(...), float(...), rand(min, max), pick(a | b | c) with expression options (quote literal text: pick("say hi" | "say nah")), sin/cos/tan (degrees), sqrt, abs. Write \$ for a literal dollar sign. Note: write 2*sin(x), not 2sin(x) — a bare s after a number is the stack suffix. A bad $...$ expression shows an error and sends nothing. Auto-detect additionally solves plain math like 32+4 or 3s outside NBT braces (never errors — unparseable text is sent as-is).
tooltip.tupenter.variables: Adds user variables. #set $name$ = value stores a value for the session (cleared on join if history reset is on); #local $name$ = value lasts only for that line and prints no notice. Use anywhere as $name$. Works mid-chain: #set $x$ = rand(1, 10) && /give @s stick $x$! Built-ins: $client.x$, $world.time$, ... plus any raw data via $client.nbt.<path>$ / $target.nbt.<path>$ (browse with /tupenter dump). See /tupenter vars.
tooltip.tupenter.loops: Adds loop directives. #repeat 5 (/say Tick $i$!) runs its (...) group 5 times with $i$ counting 1..5. #for $x$ in 1..10 step 2 (...) counts with full control. #foreach $mob$ in (zombie | skeleton | creeper) (/summon $mob$) runs once per item; ranges work too: #foreach $n$ in range(1, 10) (...). Groups nest and can contain && chains. Every loop is capped by Max Loop Iterations.
tooltip.tupenter.conditionals: Adds #if ($client.y$ > 60) (/say high) #else (/say low). The condition is any true/false expression; the (...) groups can hold full && chains and nested directives. For picking a value inside one command, use a ternary instead: /tp @s ~ ~$client.y > 60 ? 10 : 0$ ~.
tooltip.tupenter.max_loop_iterations: Upper bound for a single loop (#repeat count, #for range size, #foreach items). A loop over the limit is rejected before anything is sent.
tooltip.tupenter.silent_directive: Hides command feedback on your own screen. Start a line with #silent to silence all of it, or wrap part of a chain: #repeat 5 (#silent (/give @s stick) && /say here!). Also suppresses #set notices. Works in chat, as a command, and inside custom command bodies. The server still processes commands normally — other players are unaffected. Related: #norecord at line start keeps a line out of the resend history; #echo shows text only to you.
tooltip.tupenter.aliases: Custom commands in the format name = body. Bodies can include commands, chat messages, && chains, $...$ expressions, directives (#repeat, #if, #silent, ...), or other custom commands. Declare typed parameters before the body for real autocomplete — see /customcommand help for the full type list, optional =default params, and examples. Reference params as $name$ or $1$..$n$. Edits here and via /customcommand both take effect immediately.
tooltip.tupenter.add_command: Adds a new command row. WARNING: this reloads the screen — command text edits are kept, but unsaved changes in other tabs are discarded.
tooltip.tupenter.delete_command: Delete this custom command (takes effect immediately).
tooltip.tupenter.wrap_toggle: Toggle a larger editor with word wrap. You can use newlines to format long entries — they're saved and survive collapsing/expanding, but the entry still runs as a single line. Editing the collapsed single-line view replaces the formatted version.
message.tupenter.import_confirm: This will reload the screen and discard any other unsaved changes. Are you sure?
